question: On 7 June 2026, aircraft carrying the Defence Ministers of Greece, France and the Netherlands to the Republic of Cyprus for an official EU meeting were subjected to radio interference and unauthorised communications originating from the occupied areas of the Republic of Cyprus, while Turkish military aircraft operated in the vicinity of the flights.

These unacceptable actions raise serious concerns regarding aviation safety, constitute interference with official EU activities, and challenge the sovereignty of the Republic of Cyprus, a Member State of the EU.

They also serve as a reminder that the continued Turkish military occupation of part of the territory of the Republic of Cyprus remains a source of instability and tension in the Eastern Mediterranean, underscoring the need for the EU to consistently uphold international law and to actively support efforts aimed at ending the occupation. In the light of the above: 1.
Does the Commission condemn these actions by the Turkish occupying forces in Cyprus?
Will the Commission raise this incident in the framework of EU-Türkiye relations?
Does the Commission intend to consider concrete measures in response to such behaviour or will it continue to tolerate repeated provocations and violations directed against EU Member States?
Supporter1
This question is supported by a Member other than the authors: Emmanouil Fragkos (ECR).
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.8.2026) The Commission is aware of the reports and remain in contact with counterparts in the Republic of Cyprus. The EU has a strategic interest in a stable and secure environment in the Eastern Mediterranean and in the development of a cooperative and mutually beneficial relationship with Türkiye.

Türkiye is expected to respect international law, as well as the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all EU Member States. It is also of paramount importance that Türkiye commits to and actively contributes to a fair, comprehensive and viable settlement of the Cyprus issue, including its external aspects. These are key elements for upholding regional stability in the Eastern Mediterranean.
The EU remains committed to defending its interests and those of its Member States.
